salarySummary: Annual gross pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming 38 ordinary hours per week for full-time employees under the National Employment Standards.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,261.44 per year.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage in Australia for 2026–27?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a full-time employee working 38 hours. Casual employees receive at least $33.05 per hour, which includes a 25% casual loading. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award-free employees.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. For example, if the base rate is $26.44, the casual rate is $33.05. When using our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) tool, you enter the base rate and check the box to add 25% – do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

Whether you're earning the National Minimum Wage or negotiating a contract like Cristiano Ronaldo's salary, the principle is the same: your annual pay is your hourly rate multiplied by the hours you work each week, multiplied by 52. This simple formula helps you compare job offers, budget, and understand your entitlements.

### The Standard Full-Time Assumption

Under the National Employment Standards (NES), a full-time employee works a maximum of 38 ordinary hours per week. Most awards and enterprise agreements adopt this as the standard. Therefore, when converting an hourly rate to annual, we assume 38 hours per week unless stated otherwise. The formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,261.44 per year

This is the gross amount before tax and super. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same example:

$1,004.90 (weekly) × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) applies to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. However, most industries have modern awards that set higher minimum rates. For example, the Supported Employment Services Award [MA000103] has its own pay guide with specific classifications. Always check the relevant award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to ensure you're receiving the correct minimum rate.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour. When using our [the timesheet](/) tool, you enter your base hourly rate and tick the box to add casual loading – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

## Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an employee earning the National Minimum Wage, super would be:

$52,261.44 × 12% = $6,271.37 per year, paid by the employer.

Tax is withheld by your employer using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For the National Minimum Wage earner, tax and Medicare would be approximately $6,442 per year, leaving a take-home pay of about $45,819. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

## Even Cristiano Ronaldo's Salary Follows the Same Math

It might seem absurd to compare a footballer's earnings to the National Minimum Wage, but the underlying calculation is identical. Cristiano Ronaldo's salary, whether paid per match or per season, can be broken down into an hourly equivalent. If he earns, say, $200 million per year (a hypothetical figure), working 38 hours per week for 52 weeks would imply an hourly rate of over $100,000. Of course, his actual working hours and conditions are vastly different, but the principle of hourly × hours × 52 holds. This perspective helps illustrate how even the highest earners are ultimately compensated for their time and skill.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.
